title: The Pale Hand
blurb: A stolen ledger, and the Pale Hand already on the north road.
pitch: You are Jin, courier for the resistance. The Ledger is in your hands, and you have to reach Commander Thorne before Aldric does.

chapters.title: The Lantern Quarter
chapters.setting: Rain hammers the rooftops of Bridgeport. In the back room of a candle shop, Vera — a resistance fence with ink-stained fingers — shoves the Ledger and a smoke bomb into your hands. Bells clang. The Ash Guard sweeps the Lantern Quarter door by door, a torch on every corner. Two years ago they took your sister as a suspected sympathizer, and the eighty silver in your purse was meant for a name on a list. Vera looks at you once. "You're faster than a letter and dumber than a coward. Perfect. Go."
chapters.objective: Get the Ledger out of the Lantern Quarter before the sweep reaches Vera's door.

choices.label: Take the rooftops and go over the city wall

success.text: You take the ridge of the candle shop and run the wet tiles with the Ledger against your ribs. A loose slate kicks out and you catch the next one. The city wall is a black lip under the bells. You go over it unseen, a night ahead of the sweep.

failure.text: Your boot finds the rotten slate. You slip, crash through a fish-stall awning, and the breath goes out of you in a stink of scales. The Ledger stays in your coat. You limp clear of the quarter with the night no longer yours.

complication.text: A torch swings up onto your roof and the sweep comes with it. You run, bells eating the quarter behind, with no market and no mare on this road. The north road takes you at a dead sprint. The gorge is already in the dark ahead.

bonus.text: You clear the wall on the quiet side of the bells, a night ahead and the Ledger dry. At the gate, Vera's cousin tosses a healing potion into your hands and does not stop walking. The glass is warm from his pocket. You pocket it and keep the dark.

choices.label: Take the sewers out to the river grate

success.text: You drop through the grate behind the candle shop and take the sewer that runs to the river. The dark stinks of tar and old water. The grate at the far end gives, and the river takes the worst of it off you. You come out free, stinking, and still ahead of the bells.

failure.text: The tunnel floods to your chest. Your purse tears on a broken rung and twenty silver goes into the black water. You keep the Ledger above it with both hands. You crawl out at the river grate, poorer, the night no longer ahead.

complication.text: The sewer bellies and throws you at a storm-mouth in the north wall. You come out running, guards on the bank, no time to buy a thing. The market town is not on this road. The gorge road takes you, wet and empty-handed.

bonus.text: You read the slope of the water and take the dry ledge the whole way. Past the river, Vera's cousin tosses a healing potion and vanishes into the rain. The Ledger never dipped. You are out, and the night is still ahead.

choices.label: Bluff the gate guards as a drunk dockworker

success.text: You put a drunk dockworker's sway into your shoulders and laugh at the gate. The guards laugh you through. On the far side one of them says the Hand's taking the north road. You keep walking, and you do not look at the Ledger.

failure.text: The laugh dies when they search you and find the shape of the book. You run. A cudgel clips your shoulder on the way through the gate. You keep the Ledger and lose the easy night, bleeding toward the market road.

complication.text: The bluff holds for one breath, and then a sergeant knows your face. You bolt, and the gate becomes a chase that does not let you stop. There is no stall and no mare on the way you are driven. The north road takes you straight at the gorge.

bonus.text: They laugh you through, and someone on the wall says the Hand's taking the north road. At the last torch, Vera's cousin tosses a healing potion into your hands without breaking stride. You catch it. The quarter closes behind you a night ahead.

choices.label: Watch the patrols from Vera's window and find the seam

success.text: You watch from Vera's window until the torches make a seam, and you slip it a night ahead. A guard under the eaves is reading a letter sealed with the word Millbrook. You take the word with you and not its meaning. The quarter lets you go.

failure.text: You watch, and the seam you wanted closes before you move. You go anyway, shoulder-first, and a torch nearly names you. The Ledger stays hidden under your cloak. You reach the market road with the night no longer ahead of the sweep.

complication.text: You wait too long at Vera's window. The sweep reaches her door, and you go out the back at a run with the book clutched blind. There is no time for a market or a mare. The north road takes you, and the gorge is the first thing that will stop you.

bonus.text: You find the seam on the first pass of the torches and slide through it a night ahead. A guard's letter, sealed with the word Millbrook, catches the light as you go. At the gate, Vera's cousin tosses a healing potion and is gone. You carry the word, the glass, and the book.

chapters.title: Crosshaven Market
chapters.setting: Dawn, two days out of Bridgeport. Crosshaven is the last market before the northern hills: spice smoke, goats, and a toothless fortune-teller. Bram waves you over, beard like steel wool, and his board lists Healing Potion 25 silver, Smoke Bombs (2) 20 silver, Longsword 35 silver, Ash the fast stubborn gray mare 60 silver, Rope and Climbing Gear 15 silver. One haggle, if you spend it here. Then a road: the patrolled flat, or the pass.
chapters.objective: Leave Crosshaven with what the hills will not sell you, on one road or the other.

choices.label: Haggle Bram for rope and a potion, then take the main road

success.text: Bram's prices do not move until your voice does. You haggle the rope and a healing potion down, and the silver leaves in a thinner stack. He spits, pleased, and points you at the main road. It is the patrolled one, and it will cost you a day.

failure.text: Bram hears the haggle and does not blink. You pay full for the rope and the potion, and the silver hurts. The main road is still the one you take. Patrols will see a courier who spent too much to be quick.

complication.text: A bailiff's whistle cuts the square while your silver is still on Bram's board. You snatch the rope and run the wrong way, away from the flat. The pass takes you. Thornwood is ahead, and the bargain is left on the stall.

bonus.text: Bram grins like a man who lost on purpose and throws in a coil of good rope. The potion is in your coat, cheaper than the board. You take the main road with the morning still wide. The patrols are out there, and so are you.

choices.label: Buy the climbing rope and take the Thornwood Pass

success.text: You buy the climbing rope and do not pretend you will take the flat road. Bram counts the silver with a thumb like a rasp. The Thornwood Pass is the fast one, two days of bandits and wolves. You leave with the coil on your shoulder and the hills in your teeth.

failure.text: The rope costs what the board says, and your purse feels it. You take the pass anyway, because the main road is a day you do not have. Bram watches you go without a kindness. The wood is faster, and it is not kind.

complication.text: You have the rope in your hand when the market spills. A fight at the goat pens turns into guards, and the pass mouth shuts in the noise. You are driven onto the flat with the coil bouncing on your back. The toll bridge is the way that is left.

bonus.text: Bram sells you the rope and names a dry ledge on the pass that the wolves miss. You take the Thornwood road while the market is still lighting its fires. The coil is good hemp. The wood will test whether you can use it.

choices.label: Pay the toothless fortune-teller, then ride the main road

success.text: You pay the toothless fortune-teller, and she names Millbrook without being asked. A man has been through asking about it, tall, one glove, a voice like a shut door. It is a lead, not the secret of who lives there. You take the main road with the name and without the reason.

failure.text: The fortune-teller takes your silver and gives you fog. No village, no glove, no man. You leave her stall no wiser and take the main road because the pass feels worse with an empty warning. The patrols are the price of the flat.

complication.text: Her tent flap opens on a bailiff who heard too much of the telling. You drop the rest of the silver and run before he can ask who paid her. The main road is his. The pass takes you, unwilling and fast.

bonus.text: She will not take all the silver. She says Millbrook, and she says the man asking after it left before dawn on the flat road. You take that road behind him with the coin she refused still in your purse. Who lives there is not hers to give.

choices.label: Take the pass without stopping for anyone

success.text: You do not stop for Bram, or the fortune-teller, or the smell of spice. The pass is a cut in the hills, and you take it while the market is still a rumor of goats. Your hands fumble the reins of a hired nag that is not Ash. The wood accepts you anyway, fast and unsupplied.

failure.text: You try to leave without stopping and catch your cloak on a cart-haft in the lane. The nag startles. You keep the Ledger and lose time getting free while Bram watches, unsold. You still make the pass, later than the fast road promised, with nothing extra on your back.

complication.text: The lane out of the market is a knot of bailiffs before you can choose the pass. They turn the traffic onto the flat, and the nag goes with it. No rope, no potion, no mare of your own. The toll road has you, and the wood is a missed turning.

bonus.text: You thread the market without a word and without a purchase, and the pass opens clean. A boy throws you a heel of bread you did not pay for, then runs. The wood is ahead, bandits and wolves in it, and you are early. The Ledger knocks your ribs in time with the nag.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.setting: A stone bridge crosses a roaring gorge. An Ash Guard checkpoint holds the middle of it, and a sergeant lifts travelers' faces against wanted sketches. One sketch looks a lot like you. The Ledger is a hard shape under your cloak. The far bank is Thorne's country, if you can reach it.
chapters.objective: Get the Ledger across the gorge.

choices.label: Put silver in the sergeant's hand

success.text: The sergeant's fist closes on the silver, and he waves you across. Nailed to the bridge post, the notice reads, "Millbrook: clearance in thirty days. By order of Corvane." You hold it to the Ledger. The margin note reads, "The Hand's mother still lives there. Do NOT inform him."

failure.text: You put the silver in his hand. He pockets it and calls for backup in the same breath. The bridge fills with gray coats. They take the Ledger, and they take you.

complication.text: The bribe is in his palm when a whistle goes up from the far bank. He keeps the silver and shouts, and the bridge is no longer a crossing. You scramble off the road into the trees that eat the gorge trail. Thornwood has you, and the checkpoint does not.

bonus.text: He takes the silver and looks away one heartbeat longer than the post requires. "Millbrook: clearance in thirty days. By order of Corvane." The Ledger's margin note answers it. "The Hand's mother still lives there. Do NOT inform him."

choices.label: Bluff the sergeant with a dockworker's accent

success.text: The dockworker's accent gets a grunt, and the sergeant lets you pass. Nailed to the post: "Millbrook: clearance in thirty days. By order of Corvane." You hold the notice to the Ledger's page. "The Hand's mother still lives there. Do NOT inform him."

failure.text: They grab you. You break a wristlock and run the planks with a cut opening on your arm. The checkpoint is behind you, shouting. You are across, bleeding, and the notice on the post is a blur you do not stop to read.

complication.text: The accent slips on the sergeant's name. He reaches, you duck, and the bridge becomes a scramble down the gorge bank into trees. Thorns take your cloak. The pass has you now, and the checkpoint's sketch does not.

bonus.text: The bluff lands so well he tells you which plank creaks, and you cross on the quiet ones. "Millbrook: clearance in thirty days. By order of Corvane." You match it to the margin. "The Hand's mother still lives there. Do NOT inform him."

choices.label: Climb under the bridge on the beams

success.text: You climb the beams under the roar, clumsy and slow, and come up on the far side. The post waits above you. "Millbrook: clearance in thirty days. By order of Corvane." The margin answers, "The Hand's mother still lives there. Do NOT inform him."

failure.text: Your hands betray you on the wet beam. You fall into the shallows, swallow the river, and lose a smoke bomb to the current. You crawl out on the far bank, cut and lighter. You are across, and you did not read the post.

complication.text: The beam sheds you into the shallows under the checkpoint's boots. Gray coats wade in and haul you up by the cloak. The Ledger comes out of your coat in front of them. The bridge keeps the book, and the road keeps you.

bonus.text: You find the one dry beam and cross as if your hands belonged to someone else. The notice is close enough to read without stopping. "Millbrook: clearance in thirty days. By order of Corvane." The margin says, "The Hand's mother still lives there. Do NOT inform him."

choices.label: Draw the short sword

success.text: You draw the short sword. Two guards go down on the planks, and you ride the gap they leave. "Millbrook: clearance in thirty days. By order of Corvane." Held to the page, the margin reads, "The Hand's mother still lives there. Do NOT inform him."

failure.text: The fight is ugly and short of clean. You take a cut across the ribs and still break through, the checkpoint howling behind you. The Ledger stays in your coat because you never stopped to look. You are across, bleeding, and the post is unread.

complication.text: Your first cut goes wide, and the sergeant's whistle brings the whole post. You bail off the bridge into the thorn side of the gorge before they close the far end. The sword is still in your hand. The wood, not the ford, is where this road goes.

bonus.text: The short sword feels honest for once. You drop two guards and take the notice off its nail on the way past. "Millbrook: clearance in thirty days. By order of Corvane." The margin is waiting: "The Hand's mother still lives there. Do NOT inform him."

chapters.title: The Thornwood Ambush
chapters.setting: Ancient oaks stand strangled by thorn vines, and no birdsong comes through them. An overturned merchant cart blocks the trail, too neat to be an accident. An arrow thunks into a tree an inch from your head. A woman's voice comes down from the branches. "Horse. Weapon. Walk away." Wren leads five Ash Guard deserters in the wood, and the Ledger is still against your ribs.
chapters.objective: Get out of the wood with the Ledger.

choices.label: Stay still, count the archers, and watch

success.text: You stay still and count. Four archers, and the fifth is Wren in the branches, already watching you not run. She lets you walk, horse and weapon still yours, because you did not lie with your feet. The Ledger goes with you, and her band does not.

failure.text: You count wrong. An arrow pins your cloak to the cart, and you tear free with a line of blood on your neck. They laugh and let the horse go rather than chase you into the open. You ride out poorer in skin, and still alone.

complication.text: Stillness reads as guilt. They drop from the branches, take the sword, take the Ledger, and bind your hands with your own reins. The wood does not let you walk. Gray coats who were never far behind finish what the deserters started.

bonus.text: You count four archers and Wren before she finishes the warning, and she sees that you saw them. She nods once, and the arrows stay in the trees. You walk the horse through, untouched, her face kept. The ford is beyond the last oak.

choices.label: Talk: tell them what the Ledger holds

success.text: You tell them what the Ledger holds, and Wren's jaw tightens. "The Hand came through yesterday. Didn't touch us. Asked about Millbrook, of all places." She comes down from the branches and takes your side of the road.

failure.text: You talk, and the branches do not care. Arrows come down, one of them kisses your shoulder, and you ride the gap their reload leaves. Wren does not follow. The Ledger is still yours, and her war is not.

complication.text: The first sentence out of you is the wrong one. They hear the Magistrate in it and drop, five deserters who have not decided to be anything else. The Ledger is torn out of your coat. You leave the wood in someone else's custody.

bonus.text: Wren's jaw tightens and she comes down saying, "The Hand came through yesterday. Didn't touch us. Asked about Millbrook, of all places." White-fletched arrows fill your hand. "The Hand will know these. He trained me."

choices.label: Fight them

success.text: You fight them in the thorns and they scatter, food and a scatter of silver left in the leaves. Wren is gone up a tree you cannot climb. You take what they dropped and ride. The band has no side in this, and the ford is still ahead.

failure.text: They are better in these trees than you are with a short sword. You take a cut, and they take the smoke bomb off your belt while you are on a knee. You keep the Ledger by covering it with your body. You ride out hurt, and they keep the wood.

complication.text: The fight goes wrong in the dark between the oaks. You lose the night, and with it any chance of reaching the ford before the Hand is done there. Wren's people melt into the branches. What waits at the camp is already over.

bonus.text: You break their line in one rush and come away with their food and thirty silver in a purse that is not yours. Wren watches from a branch and does not loose. You ride out faster than you entered. The ford has not heard you yet.

choices.label: Smoke bomb and ride

success.text: You crack the smoke bomb on the cart wheel and the wood fills with white. The nag bolts, and you stay on it, blind and coughing, until the trees thin. Wren never gets a word, and she cannot join what she cannot see. The ford takes you out of the smoke alone.

failure.text: The bomb pops late, more cough than cover. Arrows hunt the noise, and one opens your sleeve. You ride through anyway, the band behind you and angry. Wren does not follow a courier who tried to blind her.

complication.text: The smoke turns back on you in a twist of wind. You lose the trail and lose the night, and you come out of the trees hours late. The Hand has already been to the ford and gone. You are riding at the end of his visit.

bonus.text: The smoke is thick and the nag is fast, and you are through before Wren can nock. A second bomb waits in the saddlebag — her doing, and no kindness in it. She will not ride with you. The ford is close, and you are early into it.

chapters.title: The Hand at the Ford
chapters.setting: Thorne's camp sits in a pine hollow above the river ford. Fog comes off the water as the camp dogs start barking. A sentry lies unconscious and unharmed. The Hand is already inside. Thorne is down, and he stands over her with a thin blade out, a white glove gleaming in the firelight. "Courier. You carry something that belongs to the Magistrate. Set it down and walk away. I don't kill people who aren't on my list."
chapters.objective: Get Thorne and the Ledger out of the ford alive.

choices.label: Draw the short sword and go at him in the fog

success.text: You draw the short sword and go at him in the fog. Steel rings, short and mean, and Aldric's footing goes on the wet stones. He drops into the ford. The white glove is still on the hand that misses the bank.

failure.text: You go at him and he is simply better. The thin blade finds you twice, and nobody in the fog is left to pull you out of the shallows. Thorne shouts your name once. The dark after that is not the camp.

complication.text: The fog eats your first cut. Thorne drags you clear by the cloak while the Hand steps back, already leaving. He walks into the white and does not run. You are alive, and so is the man you could not hold.

bonus.text: The fog hides your feet and not his glove. You catch the thin blade, turn it, and put him into the ford in one motion. Aldric goes into the water. The glove stays visible, a pale scrap on the current.

choices.label: Show him the Millbrook page and tell him about his mother

success.text: You show him the Millbrook page and say what the margin forbids. His eyes move twice over the same line. The glove shifts on his wrist. The blade lowers, and the ford goes quiet around the book.

failure.text: You show him the page and he does not believe you. Millbrook makes him go still, not kind. He hesitates long enough for Thorne to drag herself clear of the blade. Then he takes the fog, and the pause has a price.

complication.text: You lift the Ledger and he reads the motion as a weapon. The thin blade moves once. You go down in the pine needles with the book still open, and the fog fills with his people. The page never gets its second look.

bonus.text: You hold the Millbrook page in the firelight, and your voice does not crack. He reads it as if the camp has gone silent for him alone. The white glove loosens at the wrist. The book is still in your hand when he decides.

choices.label: Offer the Ledger in exchange for Thorne's life

success.text: You offer the Ledger for Thorne's life and do not dress it up. He takes the book as if it had always been his to collect. Thorne breathes. He leaves without a thank-you, and the purge list leaves with him.

failure.text: He takes the Ledger, and then he takes the purse. The bargain still holds. Thorne lives, and you are poorer by every coin the road had not already spent. He does not speak, and the book is gone.

complication.text: You offer the book and he hears a trap in the offer. The exchange never starts. His people come out of the fog behind the tent, and the Ledger is taken with your wrists already bound. Thorne's life was not the coin he wanted.

bonus.text: You set the Ledger down between his blade and Thorne, and he takes it without making you kneel. He leaves the purse, a small mercy and the only one. The book goes into his coat. The camp keeps its commander.

choices.label: Smoke bomb, then drag Thorne out of the tent

success.text: You crack the smoke bomb in the tent and drag Thorne through the white by the shoulders. The Hand's blade cuts canvas, not flesh. You hit the cold water of the ford and keep going. He does not follow into the smoke, and he is not dead.

failure.text: The bomb fumbles in your hands and bursts at your own feet. You lose Thorne's wrist in the white. When it clears, the Hand is the one holding you, and the Ledger is already out of your coat. The tent still stands.

complication.text: The smoke blows the wrong way, out over the river. You drag Thorne into the shallows after it, and the Hand follows onto wet stones he does not know. Your blade finds him where the fog cannot. He drops into the current, and the white glove goes downstream without him.

bonus.text: The bomb is clean and the drag is cleaner. Thorne comes out on your shoulder, breathing, and the Hand is only a shape in the smoke. You make the ford. He makes the fog, and the night will call that a kind of win.

endings.title: The Hand Turns
endings.text: Aldric reads the Millbrook page twice, and then he pulls the white glove off a hand that will not hold still. "She's still there. My mother." He kneels to Thorne — not surrender, an offer — and the Magistrate's best blade belongs to the resistance before the fog has finished rising. Thorne lives, and her cells have a name to answer to at last. Wren's band comes down out of the Thornwood and takes the resistance's side. The Ledger never goes back to Corvane, and the white glove curls in the campfire with nobody left to pull it out.

endings.title: The Hand Falls
endings.text: Steel flashes in the fog, and Aldric drops into the ford. His white glove drifts downstream. The resistance holds, Thorne alive in the pine hollow, and Corvane will send someone worse. The Ledger stays with you, and no one warns Millbrook. Wren's band does not march for Corvane.

endings.title: The Hand Vanishes
endings.text: Thorne lives. The Hand melts into the fog off the river, unfinished and uncaught. It is a victory with a bill attached, and your name is on the list. The Ledger stays in your coat. Wren's band is left in the open war, and the resistance keeps only what it could drag clear of his blade.

endings.title: The Courier's Bargain
endings.text: You hand the Ledger over without a word, and the purge list goes home to Corvane. Thorne's hand finds your shoulder. "We'll get it back." Wren's band waits in the Thornwood on a promise the book no longer keeps. The resistance lives, poorer by the pages that named its dead.

endings.title: Captured
endings.text: You wake in a cell in Bridgeport, straw and river-damp and the smell of cold stone. A white glove lies folded on the floor outside the bars. A voice comes out of the dark. "You nearly had it, courier." The Ledger is back in Corvane's hands, Wren's band cannot pull you out, and the resistance loses the night.
